pr_title: Enumerate available states in Prometheus startup
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The Prometheus integration listens for state changes in order to populate its internal metric table, but does not attempt to initialize that in any way. The effect of this is that any integrations initialized before the Prometheus integration does not have their states properly registered until a state change occurrs.

This change adds an enumeration over all the available states after installing the state change event listener in order to initialize the internal metric table.

issue_context.title: Prometheus doesn't expose entities after a restart until their state changes
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Very similar to https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/40431 I just encountered an issue with a very seldom changing metric. In my case, it is a helper with the current energy tariff (which changes yearly). After I updated / Restarted Home-Assistant, the metric was no longer exposed to Prometheus until I changed the value by 0.0001 (and changed it back).

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.7.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Prometheus

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/prometheus/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# Prometheus export configuration
namespace: hass
filter:
  include_entity_globs:
    - input_number.energy_tariff
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
